The framework attaches a child server under a URL prefix and makes it inherit parent settings primarily through `app.use()` and a `mount` event handler, both in the application module.

`lib/application.js` — In `app.use()`, when the given function is itself an Express app (has `.handle` and `.set`), it sets `fn.mountpath = path` (the URL prefix) and `fn.parent = this`, then registers a `mounted_app` middleware on the parent router that delegates to the child's `handle()` and restores the parent's request/response prototypes afterward. The `defaultConfiguration()` registers an `on('mount')` listener that, on mount, inherits the parent's settings by `Object.setPrototypeOf(this.settings, parent.settings)` (so the child sees parent settings via the prototype chain), inherits the trust-proxy function if the child left it at default, and links the child's `request`/`response`/`engines` prototypes to the parent's.

`lib/express.js` — `createApplication()` builds each app's `request` and `response` prototypes (with an `app` reference) so the prototype-chain inheritance performed during mount works correctly for child apps.

`lib/application.js`

The whole mechanism lives in this single file: `app.use(path, fn)` (lines ~190–244) detects a passed-in object that has both `.handle` and `.set` (i.e. a child Express app), records `fn.mountpath = path` and `fn.parent = this`, registers it on the parent's `router` under that prefix via a `mounted_app` wrapper that also restores `req.app`/`res.app` prototypes after the child finishes, and emits the `'mount'` event — while the `'mount'` handler installed in `defaultConfiguration()` (lines ~107–121) does the inheritance by setting the prototypes of the child's `request`, `response`, `engines`, and `settings` to the parent's (plus special-casing `trust proxy`), and `app.path()` (lines ~400–404) reconstructs the full prefix by walking parents.

The framework attaches a child app under a URL prefix via `app.use(path, subApp)`, which rejects the prefix onto a router and (via a wrapper middleware) delegates to the child's `handle`, restoring the parent's `req.app`/`res.app` prototypes so the child inherits the parent's settings and app chain.

The relevant files:

`lib/application.js`
`lib/router/index.js`
`lib/utils.js`
`lib/request.js`
`lib/response.js`

Why: `lib/application.js` is the core — its `app.use` mounts the child server (detected via `fn.handle`/`fn.set`), records `mountpath`/`parent`, sets up the wrapper middleware that calls `fn.handle(...)` and resets the prototypes on `req`/`res` so settings flow from the parent to the child.

The core mechanism lives in a single file, with the `router` package providing the URL-prefix routing underneath.

`lib/application.js`

This file contains both halves of the mechanism: `app.use()` detects when the passed function is an express app (it has `.handle` and `.set`), sets its `mountpath` to the URL prefix, registers a `mounted_app` middleware in the parent router that calls the child's `handle()` at that prefix, and emits a `mount` event; meanwhile `defaultConfiguration` registers an `on('mount')` handler that makes the child inherit the parent's settings by setting `Object.setPrototypeOf(this.settings, parent.settings)` (plus the request/response prototypes and engines), so the child reads up the prototype chain for any setting it does not define itself.
